Early in a thoughtful afternoon, the ramp team met a slow start Incident report: delayed departure with pet care review

The Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways logged this incident after a routine pet transfer was disrupted during boarding. The traveler arrived with Cookie in a secure carrier, and the handoff began normally. During the last check, the team noticed that one latch on the carrier was not seated as expected, so the pet was kept in a calm holding area while the carrier was inspected again. The traveler stayed nearby and cooperated with the staff, which helped keep the pet settled. No distress was reported, and the animal remained comfortable throughout the pause.

The delay then affected the departure flow because the boarding order had to be held until the carrier was confirmed safe. <<FACT F109>> The agent on duty explained the process to the traveler in plain terms, confirmed that the pet plan stayed in place, and kept watch on the carrier while the ramp team completed the check. Once the issue was corrected, the pet was returned to the travel path, and the flight proceeded without any further pet-related concern.

Handling steps were straightforward. The team completed a second visual inspection, secured the latch, checked the carrier surface for any damage, and documented the event in the trip file. The traveler was updated before release, and the companion animal remained under supervision until the final transfer point was clear. Safety stayed ahead of speed, which is the right standard for every animal move handled by the desk.

Follow-up includes a review of carrier condition notes, a reminder to staff to confirm latch security during intake, and a short check with ground handling on how the pause was managed. The desk will also keep the trip record open for any later note from the traveler. No injury, loss, or further delay was reported after the correction. Companion Animal Travel Desk
